messages:
arjun: quick follow-up on delegation: we need a private spec for the consent token lifecycle before RFC lands. thinking about revocation, short TTL, and auditable issuance.

kevin: agree. proposal: consent_token = signed JWT with fields: tenant_id, allowed_regions[], issued_at, expires_at, policy_version, issuer_kid. runtime validates signature + TTL.

marta: yubikeys for signing? we'll integrate with KMS for hosted, but private installs need attested keys or allow BYO-KMS. note this in spec.

lia: revocation is tricky. we can't check revocation list synchronously on every write (perf). options: (a) short TTLs (e.g. 5m) so revocation window small, (b) token versioning: include policy_version and check remote policy cache with soft TTL, (c) realtime revocation push via control-plane pubsub to runtimes.

arjun: prefer (a)+(c) hybrid. runtime honors short TTL AND subscribes to revocation stream for fast revokes. if stream down, short TTL bounds exposure.

kevin: how do we encode consent granularity? region-level or storage-class-level? also need reason codes for audits (e.g., emergency, scheduled_maintenance, overload).

marta: token claim allowed_regions and allowed_classes (ephemeral, persistent). reason_code lives in delegation_event log, not token. token is consent, event holds context.

lia: operational contract: when runtime receives RequestDelegation and control-plane returns allowed + token_id, runtime attaches headers: X-Delegated-Region, X-Delegation-Audit-Id, X-Delegation-Token-Id. also emit metric `delegation_decision{tenant,region,reason}`.

arjun: and we must be explicit about failure modes: if control-plane responds allowed=false -> 409 + body explaining governance reason. if control-plane unreachable -> fail-closed: return 503 or 409 depending on strictness? i think 503 is better so clients can retry.

kevin: 503 will trigger retries — dangerous for idempotency. better return 409 with message 'delegation-service-unavailable, fail-closed'. ops can configure per-tenant policy to choose fail-closed vs fail-open. default: fail-closed.

lia: add a safe-guard header for observability: X-Delegation-Status: delegated|denied|control-plane-unreachable. consumers can alert on control-plane-unreachable spikes.

arjun: testing: unit tests for JWT validation, integration tests for revocation stream (chaos), e2e with dedicated cluster enabling opt-in. include test harness to simulate cross-region latency and token expiry mid-write.

marta: sequence diagram note: client -> proxy write(propagation) -> runtime RequestDelegation -> control-plane validate -> control-plane issues token -> runtime write to sanctuary w/ delegation metadata -> control-plane log event -> replication to origin. capture timings.

kevin: replication: we must ensure delegated writes are idempotent. include delegation_id (UUIDv4) stamped by runtime and returned in responses. reconciliation uses delegation_id to dedupe.

arjun: also need to consider analytics pipelines: include delegation_audit_id in all downstream events (usage billing, cost attribution). ensure token_id ties to customer consent record.

lia: doc/console: UI to manage consent tokens: show active tokens, TTL, allowed regions, last_used, revoke button. include thumbnails for legal teams to download signed consent.

marta: rollout: alpha in dedicated with single tenant, then canary to larger set. default off for hosted; opt-in via tenant.set_delegation_consent API. include legal sign-off checklist.

kevin: security: rotate signing keys regularly; issue short-lived intermediate tokens for runtimes to validate (cacheable). support key rollover with kid header.

arjun: infra-bot: create infra ticket for pubsub channel and token endpoints.

infra-bot: created ticket INFRA-2509: "delegation consent lifecycle endpoints + revocation stream" and assigned to infra-oncall. :white_check_mark:

lia: follow-up action items: arjun draft token spec, kevin write key rotation + KMS integration doc, marta coordinate legal checklist, lia produce runbook for ops. reconvene after drafts.

arjun: I'll sketch the proto and a sample JWT claim set and post to #architecture later today.

kevin: tiny ask: add metric `delegation_revokes_count` and alert if >0 for hosted customers — suspicious unless expected.

marta: noted. thanks everyone.
